title: been working diligently for the past few weeks to build a rendering pipeline
author: cool_fox
selftext:
I'm working on a game in space and to acheive a certain level of ambiance and immersion I need a very particular environment rendered. So to that end I've been trying to develop a webgpu approach to rendering beautiful (high fidelity and structurally realistic) nebula. and it's been quite difficult, so much so I went ahead and made this its own project. I didn't realize how novel of an effort this was.

Anyways I managed to get to a decent enough state now that I feel comfortable sharing it with others.

I originally took inspiration from games like starsector and starcom but got to the point where, 1) I didn't want to simply copy what they did. 2) when you over analyze this stuff you begin to find ways to nit-pick good things so I basically wanted to get something nicer than what I was originally going for (scope creep). 3) this needs to run in a browser, performantly.

my endstate goals shifted to images like these  
[https://app.astrobin.com/i/5a6jbl#fullscreen](https://app.astrobin.com/i/5a6jbl#fullscreen)  
[https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/nebula/en/nebula1.en.jpg](https://spaceplace.nasa.gov/nebula/en/nebula1.en.jpg)

I'm not there yet but I'm getting pretty close. For those interested here's a link to some of the research I did, it'll give you an idea of what my current architecture is and what direction I went: [https://chatgpt.com/share/69fd37a4-9a2c-83e8-a2b6-3246157c0be8](https://chatgpt.com/share/69fd37a4-9a2c-83e8-a2b6-3246157c0be8)

comments.author: SuperLik69
comments.body: Very good work, looking forward to seeing more.

comments.author: lordhiggsboson
comments.body: An actual rendering pipeline from scratch or are you using three.js?

replies.author: cool_fox
replies.body:
Explicitly avoiding three.js (though taking some inspiration from a project or two). It is from scratch. It's taken alil over a month but this week I got to a pretty good place.

'Ive developed a set of "tools" or rendering methods that align to how I think a nebula should be produced. From there, I'm creating presets to sort of prove out how to build some popular nebula types using these tools and to allow my coding agents to know how to use the tools without my guidance. After I get the presets locked down I'll probably start working towards procedural nebula gen, then making performant, then getting exports for my game that don't require the full pipeline.

I don't want to share the rendering details yet because bigger projects could adopt it and I'm looking to keep some differentiators so I can compete with others.
